title: SPEAK & SIP: Language Exchange
description: This time our theme is **Fashion & Style** — clothes we love (or regret), personal style, trends that come and go, and how fashion looks completely different depending on the country or culture. We’ll talk about how we choose what to wear, whether style is self-expression or social pressure, and how fashion reflects identity, profession, gender, or generation. From iconic national looks to questionable trends we secretly tried, this theme is perfect for cultural comparison, storytelling, and light but meaningful discussion. Our languages: English, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, and German. At Speak & Sip, we do things a little differently. There’s structure — but the atmosphere is still relaxed. Think of it as semi-serious, semi-casual: fun and social, but with the clear purpose of improving our language skills. Here’s how it works: • **Each language has its own table** with a host or fluent speakers to guide the group. • **Native speakers** are always welcome to join their table and support learners. • For the **first hour**, we use conversation cards on the theme to keep things flowing. You’ll switch partners regularly so you can practice with different people. • The **second hour** is dedicated to games related to the theme — light, interactive, and designed to make everyone speak more. If you want something lighter, there will also be an **English chill table** where people can sit together and talk about any topic. But if your goal is to practice languages in a structured way, this is the right meetup for you. Our aim is simple: to connect through language, to learn from each other, and to make progress while enjoying good company. **[Join us on WhatsApp](https://chat.whatsapp.com/BWIfXe0dCFN7RMPt6NG7Mk)** **Follow the community: @forvm.lisbon** ATTENTION This is a **free event**, but to support the venue we kindly ask everyone to **order at least one drink** (even just water). Too often, founders work on ideas that can never make it, no matter how passionate they are. Problems might be a twisted market, wrong perception of user needs, the fact that it has been tried x times before and always failed, and many other caveats that are best identified BEFORE starting to put serious effort into an idea. That's why "Christoph's Feedback" is a monthly event to either a) show and tell your startup or product idea in order to get tough feedback BEFORE you begin to seriously put work and money into it or start fundraising. The feedback you get might either be a strong suggestion to reconsider or even fold your idea - or highly valuable advice on the next most useful steps to turn it into reality. There's no need for you to prepare a slide deck or follow any "elevator pitch" rule; just tell us what you're working on or b) come as a guest to hear what other founders in Berlin are working on, learn how to discover critical challenges and questions about ideas yourself, and maybe even join the team of an idea you particularly like.
